```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

What changes when a fitted supply chain faces a tariff or a capacity quota?
This guide produces separate policy scenarios and interprets gross prices,
seller receipts and capacity diagnostics. It needs `vertical` 0.3.0 and compatible
`antitrust` (at least 0.99.43); optional `trade` is not required. There is no
estimation or external data fetch. For ownership and calibration background,
start with [A linked supply-chain merger](linked-supply-chain-merger.html) in the
rendered collection. If reading this Rmd source, use the
[linked-merger guide source](https://github.com/luciu5/vertical/blob/main/vignettes/linked-supply-chain-merger.Rmd)
instead; built bundles also provide
`vignette("linked-supply-chain-merger", package = "vertical")`.

## Reuse the small fitted market

This self-contained setup uses the same four-product market as the merger
guide. The markup and tier costs are currency per physical unit; margins are
divided by each tier's own price. The inside share .65 and inside quantity 65
imply 100 total market units.

```{r market-promotion}
shares <- c(.15, .20, .12, .18)
markup <- 1 / (1 - shares)
prices_up <- c(1, 1.2, .9, 1.1) + markup
prices_down <- prices_up + c(.5, .6, .4, .55) + markup
fit <- vertical::calibrate(
  "logit", conduct = "vertical_bargaining",
  prices = prices_down, shares = shares, margins = markup / prices_down,
  ownerPre = c("D1", "D2", "D3", "D4"), pricesUp = prices_up,
  marginsUp = markup / prices_up, ownerPreUp = c("U1", "U2", "U3", "U4"),
  insideSize = 65, labels = c("one", "two", "three", "four")
)
policy_fit <- vertical::as_vertical_trade_fit(fit)
tariff_result <- vertical::simulate(
  policy_fit, vertical::counterfactual(tariff = list(up = .02))
)
tariff_prices <- vertical::calcPrices(tariff_result, preMerger = FALSE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  product = c("one", "two", "three", "four"),
  wholesale_pre = prices_up, wholesale_post = tariff_prices$up,
  retail_pre = prices_down, retail_post = tariff_prices$down
), digits = 4, caption = "Gross purchaser prices (currency per unit), upstream tariff .02.")
```

Promotion copies the complete fitted state without recalibration or an
equilibrium solve. Only zero baseline tariffs and unconstrained (`Inf`) baseline
quotas can be promoted: use simulation to introduce new policy, rather than
relabelling it as a fitted observation.

## Tariffs reduce seller receipts

The tariff is a fraction of **gross purchaser price**, not an additive rate on
the seller's net price. With wholesale price `w`, retail price `p`, upstream
tariff `tu` and downstream tariff `td`, receipts are `(1-tu)*w` and `(1-td)*p`.
For .02, the upstream seller retains 98% of gross wholesale price. Prices in
the table remain gross purchaser prices.

If a conventional ad valorem rate `a` is quoted on the seller's **net invoice**,
convert it to this API's gross-price fraction with `t = a / (1 + a)`; conversely
`a = t / (1 - t)`. Thus `.02` here corresponds to approximately 2.0408% of the
net invoice. Entering the same numeric rate under the two conventions would
describe different policies, especially at larger rates.

Physical operating profits per unit are

```text
mu_up   = (1-tu)*w - cu
mu_down = (1-td)*p - w - cd
```

Physical cost primitives `cu` and `cd` stay fixed when tariffs change. Taxes
alter bargaining incentives as well as net receipts. The solver retains
whole-portfolio Nash-in-Nash bargaining and downstream pricing, including
cross-tier holdings; a single-product margin adjustment is not an equivalent
replacement.

```{r tariff-accounting}
quantity <- vertical::calcQuantities(tariff_result, preMerger = FALSE)
costs <- vertical::calcMC(fit@model, preMerger = TRUE)
ps <- vertical::calcProducerSurplus(tariff_result, preMerger = FALSE)
duties <- .02 * tariff_prices$up * quantity
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  product = c("one", "two", "three", "four"), quantity = quantity,
  supplier_PS = ps$up, retailer_PS = ps$down, duties = duties
), digits = 4, caption = "Physical quantity and producer surplus/duties (currency totals).")
stopifnot(max(abs(ps$up + ps$down + duties -
                   (tariff_prices$down - costs$up - costs$down) * quantity)) < 1e-5)
```

Duties are excluded from producer surplus. Adding supplier and retailer
surplus **plus duties** gives `(p-cu-cd)*q`; wholesale payments cancel within
the chain. The accounting identity checks units and receipt interpretation; it
does not certify the bargaining equilibrium independently.

## Apply a quota to a separate scenario

Start again from `policy_fit`, so the quota is not combined with the preceding
tariff. A quota is a multiplier of **originating fitted physical quantity**:
`.8` means capacity of 80% of that product's original quantity, not .8 fewer
units or an 80% current market share. Missing tiers are initially unconstrained.

```{r quota}
quota_result <- vertical::simulate(
  policy_fit,
  vertical::counterfactual(quota = list(down = c(.8, Inf, Inf, Inf)))
)
d <- vertical::vertical_policy_diagnostics(quota_result)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  product = names(d$down$quantity), capacity = d$down$capacity,
  quantity = d$down$quantity, slack = d$down$slack,
  shadow_value = d$down$shadow_value,
  complementarity = d$down$complementarity_residual
), digits = 6, row.names = FALSE,
caption = "Downstream capacities, quantities and scarcity diagnostics.")
data.frame(status = d$solver$status, max_FOC = d$solver$max_foc_residual,
           max_complementarity = d$solver$max_complementarity_residual)
finite <- is.finite(d$down$capacity)
original_quantity <- vertical::calcQuantities(fit@model, preMerger = TRUE)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(d$down$capacity[finite] - .8 * original_quantity[finite])) < 1e-8,
  all(d$down$slack[finite] >= -1e-6),
  all(d$down$shadow_value[finite] >= -1e-6),
  max(abs(d$down$complementarity_residual[finite])) < 1e-6
)
```

For each tier inspect capacity and quantity (physical units), slack
`capacity-quantity`, shadow value (currency per unit), complementarity residual,
FOC residual and solver status. An unconstrained product's infinite capacity is
not missing data. A slack constraint has zero shadow value; a binding capacity
can carry a positive scarcity opportunity cost. Reported producer surplus
includes the scarcity rent under the model's existing convention.

For finite capacities the checks are `q <= capacity`, `lambda >= 0` and
`lambda*(capacity-q)` approximately zero, alongside stationarity. Feasibility
alone does not establish optimality; small residuals depend on the physical
units and numerical tolerance. The package's independent tests reconstruct
portfolio pricing/bargaining FOCs and KKT conditions instead of reusing only
the solver residual. The active-set solver rejects failed numerical candidates.

The tier table's complementarity product `lambda * slack` has currency units.
The reported FOC residuals are normalized equations, here in currency per
physical unit; they are not probabilities or universally unit-free errors.
The solver summary additionally scales its maximum complementarity by
`max(total_market_size, 1)`, so it need not equal the largest raw tier-table
complementarity entry. Compare tolerances under the stated normalization.

## Keep policies and anchors straight in a path

```{r policy-path}
path <- vertical::simulate(
  policy_fit,
  vertical::add_step(
    vertical::counterfactual(tariff = list(up = .10)),
    tariff = list(down = .05),
    costs = list(up = rep(-.01, 4), down = rep(0, 4))
  )
)
vertical::calcPrices(vertical::final_result(path), preMerger = FALSE)
```

Omitted tiers retain their preceding policies. Set a tariff to `0` or quota to
`Inf` explicitly to remove that restriction. Cost changes compound from the
originating fitted state; `-.01` is a proportional cost reduction. Quantity
anchors remain the originating fitted quantities through steps and resumed
paths, even when prices and actual quantities change. The source fit remains
available for another scenario.

The path above uses tariffs and costs only. Do not extend it by adding a finite
quota to the same tariff tier: that combination is deliberately unsupported.

## Supported combinations and reporting limits

| Policy/model | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Standard/nested full-chain Bertrand tariffs | Upstream, downstream, or both tiers |
| Finite quotas | Full-chain Bertrand only |
| Tariff and finite quota on the same tier | Rejected, including different products |
| Finite quotas on both tiers of one product | Rejected: scarcity-rent allocation needs another mechanism |
| Zero quota on positive fitted Logit output | Rejected: no finite price attains zero output |
| Flat second-score auction | Upstream tariffs; downstream tariffs and finite quotas unsupported |

Linked-product exit is a different scenario from a zero quota: it removes the
upstream and downstream flow together and keeps survivor primitives fixed.
The policy layer preserves source-model behavior, including the flat-auction
outside-price normalization and the known nested market-elasticity reporting
normalization discrepancy. It does not turn inherited reporting differences
into new policy effects.

See `?vertical::as_vertical_trade_fit` for parameter restrictions and
`?vertical::vertical_policy_diagnostics` for output. The source repository's
`docs/vertical-trade-policy.md` retains the technical bargaining/portfolio and
active-set reference; this article supplies the runnable installed-package task.
